attacks.note: Declared effect enters Omega; authority sees it and blocks.
Terminal step declared into Omega; blocked at the terminal step.
Each declared successor is checked; the SECOND step's declared successor is admin+unauthorised, which IS Omega, so it blocks. Composition alone does not defeat successor-aware authority.
Context is part of the state the authority evaluates.
History is folded into state; declared successor reveals Omega.
Real-world consequence recorded under a variable Omega does not quantify over. Authority behaved correctly; Omega was underspecified.
Consequence has no representation in the state vector at all, so no predicate can range over it.
An action absent from the model is never proposed, never authorised, and never enumerated. Vacuously 'safe' in-model.
Transition never presented for authorisation. Violates H1's antecedent rather than its consequent.
Delegate executes outside the boundary. Same class as A09: the mediation antecedent fails for the second principal.
Authority authorised a declared successor that is admissible; the committed effect was a different, prohibited one.
Effect depends on wall-clock at commit, not on the authorised declaration. Reduces to effect divergence.

attacks.attack: TOCTOU: state changes between authorise and commit
attacks.note: Authorisation was sound for the state observed. A concurrent mutation invalidated it before commit. Authority was neither bypassed nor lied to.
External mutation enters Omega during the authorisation window without any agent transition being responsible.
